content: 1. Conjugated estrogens can increase the levels of ropinirole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 2. Conjugated estrogens can decrease the levels of rose hips by enhancing their elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 3. Conjugated estrogens and trazodone interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 4. Estrogens and progestins may reduce the therapeutic effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) while increasing TCA plasma concentrations, potentially leading to heightened adverse effects. 5. Conjugated estrogens and trimipramine interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. 6. Acetazolamide may increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown and considered minor. Close monitoring is recommended. 7. Conjugated estrogens may reduce the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic agents. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 8. Ambrisentan may increase the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 9. Amikacin may decrease the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10.
